source: Bible Q3.2 tables (Q3-decision-response-battery.md), transcribed by script; claim and basisText are the bible's words. basisStatus is read from basisText. PA-1 claims every coverage family and its text gives 2 of 3 for Cover 3 only and 1 of 3 otherwise, so the row carries the weaker 1 of 3. SC-1 and CR-2 say 2 of 3. GM-2, GM-4 and GM-5 are arithmetic from rule values and the engine's own rates.

items.claim: Play action raises expected points per dropback against every coverage family
items.basisText: Measured +0.07 to +0.13 in one dataset; one outside source agrees on direction for Cover 3 only. Direction 2 of 3 (Cover 3), 1 of 3 otherwise. Size not asserted

items.claim: Play action's gain does not depend on a high run rate beforehand by more than a small band
items.basisText: Active. No measurable dependence on earlier run rate or run success: interaction no larger than about 0.04 expected points, not distinguishable from zero (J15 item 3, `research/audit-r-pa-definitions.md` R28). 1 of 3 for the size: published work read second-hand

items.claim: Against five or more rushers, quick game gains value relative to its own value against four, and slow-developing concepts lose value
Screens are not a general answer to pressure: against five or more rushers a screen does not beat the average dropback
items.basisText: Two charting sources agree on direction, disagree on size (about -0.15 and about 0.00 expected points). 2 of 3

items.claim: A screen beats a pressure when the rush vacates the screen side
Four verticals stresses three-deep coverage at the seams more than two-deep man
Two-deep zone is stressed in the deep middle and the holes outside; flood stresses the flat defender in three-deep
Mesh and crossers gain against man relative to zone
items.basisText: Convention-based. Targeted-route data may order only

items.claim: Deeper throws have lower completion rate and higher yards per completion, monotonic by depth band
items.basisText: Unverified general knowledge. To be measured from the project's nflverse play-by-play (R3.2.1) before it counts

items.claim: Pressure rate rises with each added rusher from four to six
items.basisText: Measured 27% with four to 44% with six in one dataset; no outside source by rusher count. 1 of 3

items.claim: Expected points allowed when sending six stays inside a band around neutral against four
A rusher the protection rules did not account for arrives sooner than any blocked rusher
Keeping an extra blocker in lowers pressure rate and lowers the number of receivers out
Time to throw longer than the protection's hold raises sack and pressure rate monotonically
Yards per carry falls as the box goes from six to seven to eight
A loaded box raises the value of play action and outside throws
An unblocked defender at the point of attack lowers the run's success rate more than one away from it
A double team at the point of attack moves the down lineman more than a single block of equal grades
Spreading the formation lightens the box when the defence matches receivers
A correctly read option beats the same run without the read against the same front
items.basisText: Convention-based. Run-pass option passing samples are not used

items.claim: Going for it on fourth and short near midfield raises win probability relative to punting
items.basisText: Romer 2006 (primary paper, partly read; 1998 to 2000 data). 1 of 3. Public fourth-down models agree by general knowledge but none was read: Unverified. Size tunable

items.claim: Two-point and extra-point choices follow the standard score-differential logic given the engine's own conversion rates
items.basisText: Arithmetic from measured rates. Rates carry their own statuses (B7)

items.claim: A timeout kept for the end of a half is worth more than one spent early for a non-critical reason
Kneeling when the clock can be run out never loses to running a play

items.claim: Spiking costs a down and saves the time the rule set says it saves; hurrying to the line without a spike saves a down at a time cost
items.basisText: Rule-based, per rule set (the college clock stops differ: B13)

items.claim: A higher pass rate on early downs does not lower expected points for an average offense
items.basisText: Kovash and Levitt 2009, old sample. 1 of 3. Marked provisional

items.claim: Low install readiness produces more mental errors and pre-snap penalties than high readiness
Installing more than the team can absorb in a week lowers execution of the whole plan
A repeated tendency loses value over a game against an opponent who has scouted it
Breaking a strong tendency once it is established gains value relative to the same call with no tendency
A disguised coverage raises the quarterback's error rate relative to the same coverage shown early, more for a less experienced quarterback
Fatigue from long drives and tempo lowers the defensive front's contest results
The spread of results between better and worse AI coaches is wider on weak rosters than on strong ones
items.basisText: Holcomb, Holmes, Connelly 2009 by secondary summary. 1 of 3

items.basisText: Two soccer studies; NFL descriptive only. 2 of 3 soccer, 1 of 3 weak NFL
